//: WHERE THE WORD IS NOT THE PLUGIN. A handful of this package's files spell another row's name as ordinary code, and each is recorded here rather than excused by a pattern — the equality in @olai/bundle's fence.test.ts is what refuses a NEW collision until somebody writes it down with a reason. 'search' is `url.searchParams`, which every one of the three files uses because they all compose or parse a request; 'git' is the `git:` line of the version string the fake binary prints, which the pinned Himalaya really does print (`himalaya --version` ends with two lines about the build and its revision) and which the fake must reproduce or the surface check's parse is exercised over a string no binary would answer; 'vault' is the English word in the panel row's own sentence to a person — the refresh token is kept in this serve's memory, never in the vault — which is the product's word for the served directory and also a row's name.
//tools: Mail query, trash verbs and PDF attachment fixtures are mail vocabulary, not dependencies on those plugin rows.
//enclosures: A MIME type is not a row. `src/enclosures.ts` holds the small extension table a draft's attachments are typed from, so it spells `text/csv`, `text/markdown`, `image/*` and `application/pdf` — media types Gmail reads, and a table this plugin keeps itself precisely so a draft does not differ between machines. `src/tools.ts` spells `application/pdf` as the example in the argument's own description, and 'vault' as the place an agent is told it may attach a file from, which is the product's word for the served directory and also a row's name.
